mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for two consecutive months, it signals accommodative monetary policy that lowers real borrowing costs, boosting equity valuations and driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling mean during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests labor market strengthening, which typically precedes equity market optimism and positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
regime_hint: Early stage of labor market recovery
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day ahead returns are not significantly above the 30-day rolling average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 2% for three consecutive months indicates strengthening supply-side demand, which is associated with positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns as market anticipates corporate earnings strength.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the INDPRO trigger (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months, while GDP deflator remains flat, suggests disinflation and reduced policy uncertainty, which can produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as market pricing in weaker growth.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day rolling mean during the trigger (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of residential investment to GDP (not directly observable here) would be inferred from housing starts (HOUST) rising above 1.5% growth for two months, it implies future capital spending and positive 20-day S&P 500 returns under normal policy settings.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly growth > 1.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward returns during the trigger period (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% followed by a sustained rise in job openings (implied by PAYEMS) suggests tight labor markets, which can precede short-term negative 5-day S&P 500 returns as over-supply of buyers cools valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in retail sales proxy (not directly available; using GDPC1 as a broad demand indicator) of over 3% for two months signals weakening consumer demand, which is associated with negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate earnings weakness.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly decline > 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day rolling mean during the trigger (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls by more than 2% in two consecutive months, it indicates softening supply-side activity and often precedes negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as market anticipates earnings compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly decline > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative during the trigger (t-test p > 0.05).
